sources.title: Refund permissions and limitations
sources.section: Permission requirements; eligible payment types; cash and card limits

sources.title: Issuing a refund

claims.capability: An order can contain one or multiple checks, with order-level dining and handoff information.
claims.merchant_outcome: Represent a party's purchase and route each check separately while retaining the order's dining option and fulfillment context.
claims.trigger: Create or update an order for a guest.
claims.behavior: The platform associates selected items, prices, taxes, discounts, service charges, guest information and payments with checks; the order records dining option and employee, plus table, delivery, or curbside details when applicable.
claims.preconditions: Toast order is created; applicable location and dining option are configured.
claims.qualifiers: The source describes the data model, not every POS action for splitting, seating, or editing checks.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: An order may have multiple checks; exact operational split/recombine behavior is unresolved.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Make parent order, guest-visible balance, and each payer's sub-check legible throughout a multi-person checkout.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Let a guest pay a chosen check or share directly to a merchant-controlled Bitcoin endpoint while leaving cash and card available for everyone else.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Payment settlement and confirmation timing differ from card authorization; splitting, item allocation, tips and tax reconciliation need explicit rules. Do not require wallet use or conversion.
claims.acceptance_test: For an order with multiple checks, pay one check in Bitcoin and another in cash/card; verify each check's exact due amount, tip/tax treatment, open/paid state, merchant receipt and reconciliation remain correct.

claims.capability: A POS-created order is replicated to other Toast devices on the same network and can be updated on another device.
claims.merchant_outcome: Allow staff to continue handling an order from another in-network POS device.
claims.trigger: Create an order on a Toast POS device.
claims.behavior: The platform automatically replicates the order to other devices in the same network.
claims.preconditions: Toast POS devices share the same network.
claims.qualifiers: Does not establish behavior for offline devices, different networks, or third-party devices.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Offline device replication/resynchronization details are not documented on this inspected page.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Surface order-sync state and last-updated time so staff can identify stale screens during handoffs.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Keep tender state synchronized with the order state across devices; do not depend on Bitcoin to replace order replication.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: Payment settlement events can arrive asynchronously; duplicate or stale payment state can cause repeated collection risk.
claims.acceptance_test: Update an order from a second in-network device while a Bitcoin payment is pending and confirm all devices show one pending payment and one final settled/failed result.

claims.capability: Order firing to kitchen may be immediate or delayed for scheduled, approval-required, or throttled online orders.
claims.merchant_outcome: Control when an order enters preparation and manage workload surges.
claims.trigger: Create a scheduled, approval-gated, or throttled order.
claims.behavior: Scheduled orders fire at prep time; approval-required online orders fire upon approval; throttled online orders fire after the configured throttle period. Most other orders fire when created.
claims.preconditions: Relevant scheduling, approval, or throttling workflow is configured.
claims.qualifiers: API orders are not subject to online-order approval. Kitchen preparation details belong to the kitchen-operations scope.
claims.recovery_edge_cases: Firing timing depends on order source and configured delay; customer-visible estimates may diverge if preparation timing changes.
claims.improvement_hypothesis: Show staff and guests the payment state separately from kitchen firing so payment confirmation does not accidentally imply preparation has begun.
claims.bitcoin_hypothesis: Support Bitcoin payment before or after firing according to merchant policy, with clear pending state and no automatic kitchen release until the merchant's chosen acceptance threshold.
claims.bitcoin_tradeoffs: On-chain confirmation may take longer than an authorization; Lightning settlement can be fast but needs reliable invoice/payment state. Merchant should choose the rule.
claims.acceptance_test: Configure a scheduled order and an approval-required online order; verify a Bitcoin payment's pending/settled state does not bypass the configured firing time or approval gate.

claims.capability: Staff can transfer a single check or order to a clocked-in employee.
claims.merchant_outcome: Reassign service responsibility across shifts while retaining the order record.
claims.actor: Employee with transfer permission or manager

limitations: All conclusions are documentary claims from public Toast Platform Guide content inspected on 2026-11-17 (English, United States); none are tested compatibility claims.
Assigned service scope is broad. Reviewed units are only those listed in coverage; unresolved items must be researched before claiming exhaustive branch coverage.

Table/seats, hold/send/fire POS operations, split-check mechanics, transfer edge cases beyond one page, receipt page details, tax/service-charge calculations, tips/adjustments, guest credits, offline tender-specific handling, and dedicated order/payment failure pages remain uninspected.

No plan/subscription entitlement matrix, location-specific contract, device list, processor configuration, state/country legal configuration, or merchant account was available. A device or workflow condition is recorded only where the cited page states it.
Toast documentation may distinguish POS, web, online-order channels, third-party channels, hardware and permissions; claims do not imply that all Toast merchants have each capability enabled.

Bitcoin concepts are hypotheses for product research, not claims of Toast compatibility. A Bitcoin-first question should ask whether the merchant wants guest-directed on-chain or Lightning payment for any step and what confirmation, refund, tip, tax, and reconciliation rules are acceptable. Preserve merchant key control, avoid mandatory custody or forced conversion, and continue supporting cash and third-party card tenders.
